answer: The Hardware security key bound by one-time code delivery with revocation on transfer makes the identity prove its channel on demand: the hardware security key answers a fresh challenge, the one-time code delivery is recorded, and revocation on transfer keeps one channel from spawning many identities, so a rented or borrowed channel cannot quietly serve ten identities. Trust here is built the way a delta is built: slowly, binding by binding, and easy to lose. From the ledge to the lantern, the same rule holds: no channel, no trust, no exception.
